chunks: Three - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn from al-Qasim from Aban from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him saying: 'Whoever buys something from the khums, God will not excuse him, for he has bought what is not permissible for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying items from khums according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of Chapter 39 on 'Additions' (al-Ziyadat), this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq warns that purchasing items from the khums without proper authorization or distinction between the Imam's share and the general believers' share constitutes consuming unlawful property. This ruling underscores the strict legal boundaries surrounding khums assets, particularly the portion reserved for the Imam (or the Marja') during the Occultation, emphasizing that unauthorized acquisition is not merely a transactional error but a spiritual transgression for which God offers no excuse.
